theory: A wire carrying a current $I$ across a magnetic field $B$ feels a force $F = BIl$ at right angles to both. With an alternating current the force alternates at the supply frequency $f$, so the wire is forced to vibrate at $f$.
When the natural frequency of the stretched length $l$ matches $f$, the wire resonates in its fundamental mode:
A graph of $l^2$ against the tension $T = Mg$ is a straight line through the origin with slope $k = 1/(4f^{2}\mu)$, so $f = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{k\mu}}$.
The magnet must be at the middle of the vibrating length, where the fundamental has its antinode; a non-magnetic wire is used so the force alternates at $f$ and not $2f$.

apparatus.sonometer: Sonometer: wooden box with a brass wire over two bridges and a pulley.
apparatus.transformer: Step-down transformer: low-voltage alternating supply from the mains.
apparatus.magnet: Horseshoe magnet: its poles straddle the wire.
apparatus.rider: Paper rider to show the point of maximum vibration.
apparatus.masses: Hanger (0.5 kg) and 0.25 kg slotted masses.
apparatus.rule: Metre rule fixed along the sonometer.

safety: Use only the low-voltage output of the step-down transformer; never connect the wire to the mains directly.
Switch the supply off between readings so the wire does not overheat.
steps: Hang a load on the wire and record its mass M. Note μ from the label on the wire's reel.
Place the horseshoe magnet so its poles straddle the wire near the middle of the bridges.
Switch on the low-voltage AC supply.
Adjust the movable bridge until the wire vibrates with maximum amplitude and the rider is thrown off: l₁ (from short), then l₂ (from long).
Keep the magnet and rider at the middle of the new length each time.
Repeat for at least five different loads.
Work out T = Mg, l = (l₁ + l₂)/2 and l², then plot l² against T.
tips: Move the magnet whenever you change the length a lot: it must sit at the middle of the vibrating part.
Read the bridge position in the eye-level view.
Use g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹ when working out T.
references: Young, H. D. & Freedman, R. A. University Physics, ch. 27 (force on a current-carrying conductor) and ch. 15 (standing waves).
Physics Bench virtual laboratory — AC sonometer practical.

massNotTension.title: T is the tension in newtons, not the mass
massNotTension.detail: Multiply the mass in kilograms by g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹: a 1.50 kg load gives T = 14.7 N.

magnetOffCentre.title: The magnet was off-centre at {n} resonance(s)
magnetOffCentre.detail: The fundamental is driven hardest when the magnet sits at the middle of the vibrating length. Off-centre, the wire may resonate weakly or in another mode.
